Belarusian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

кра́н • (krán) m inan (genitive кра́на, nominative plural кра́ны)

  1. tap
    • 1876, Mark Twain, Прыгоды Тома Соўэра (The Adventures of Tom Sawyer):
      На́шы хло́пчыкі падстаўля́лі галаву́ пад кран, каб асвяжы́цца.
      Nášy xlópčyki padstawljáli halavú pad kran, kab asvjažýcca.
      Some of us pumped on our heads.
      (literally, “Our boys put their heads under the taps to freshen themselves.”)
  2. crane (machine)

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has articles on:
кран (машина) and кран (приспособление)
Wikipedia bgWikipedia bg

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [kran]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -an
  • Homophone: Кран (Kran)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian кран (kran), from Dutch kraan.

Noun

[edit]

кран • (kran) m (diminutive кра́нче)

  1. faucet, tap (a device for starting and stopping liquid or gas from a tank/pipeline)
    Synonyms: кане́ла (kanéla), кла́пан (klápan), чеп (čep)
    завъ́ртам (отва́рям/затва́рям) кра́н на чешма́ ― zavǎ́rtam (otvárjam/zatvárjam) krán na češmá ― to turn (on/off) a sink's faucet

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from German Kran.

Noun

[edit]

кран • (kran) m

  1. crane (machine for lifting and moving loads; forklift)
    Кра́нът разтова́рва парахо́да.
    Kránǎt raztovárva parahóda.
    The crane unloads the steamer.

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
кран
Wikipedia ru

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • кранъ (kran) — pre-1918 spelling
  • крант (krant)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Dutch kraan or from Low German kran. Cognate to German Kran (“crane”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [kran]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -an

Noun

[edit]

кран • (kran) m inan (genitive кра́на, nominative plural кра́ны or краны́*, genitive plural кра́нов or крано́в*, relational adjective краново́й or кра́новый, diminutive кра́ник) (* professional usage)

  1. (engineering) valve (a ball valve, a plug valve, or similar rotating device controlling flow through a pipe)
  2. faucet, tap, spigot
    • 1852, Лев Толстой [Leo Tolstoy], “Глава II. Maman”, in Детство; English translation from Leo Wiener, transl., Childhood, 1904:
      Ма́тушка сиде́ла в гости́ной и разлива́ла чай; одно́й руко́й она́ приде́рживала ча́йник, друго́ю — кран самова́ра, из кото́рого вода́ текла́ че́рез верх ча́йника на подно́с.
      Mátuška sidéla v gostínoj i razlivála čaj; odnój rukój oná pridérživala čájnik, drugóju — kran samovára, iz kotórovo vodá teklá čérez verx čájnika na podnós.
      Mother was sitting in the drawing-room and pouring out tea. With one hand she held the teapot, with the other the faucet of the samovár, from which the water ran over the teapot to the tray.
  3. (machine) crane
